| [ARG-200](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-200.md) | Cassi's theorem → spectral dimension sets order | [CLAIM-842](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-842.md) supposes that a Gaussian elastic energy on an interaction graph of spectral dimension d_s ≤ 2 makes long-wavelength fluctuations diverge, "the lower critical dimension of the Mermin–Wagner theorem read on a learned manifold", citing [LIT-2985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2985.md) unread. The graph version exists: Cassi (1992), after Hattori, Hattori and Watanabe (1987), proves that spectral dimension at most 2 excludes spontaneous magnetization for O(n) and Heisenberg models (as Gelfert and Nolting report it), and Nachtergaele's proof needs no translation invariance. But the theorem needs a continuous symmetry generated by a sum of local generators, equilibrium through the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, and finite second moments (Halperin), and it has exceptions (orientational order in 2D crystals, tethered membranes); Toner and Tu show the 2D logarithm of the linear theory removed out of equilibrium. So the supposition's mathematics is a held theorem, its application to a representation still supposed. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
